questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (3)** i.e. **'Harmony'.**

__
 
• **Feud:** (झगड़ा) A prolonged and bitter quarrel or conflict, often between families, groups, or individuals.

• **Harmony: **(सामंजस्य) A state of peaceful coexistence, agreement, or cooperation.
 
 
• **Example: **We should always maintain ***harmony ***by openly communicating and supporting each other through both joys and challenges.
 
 

*Therefore, the correct answer is **'Harmony'.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** The sailors faced **peril **as their ship was caught in a violent storm at sea.

• **Example:** Despite his age, he continued to exercise regularly and had the **vigour **of a much younger person.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Professor said that __I will be late for the lecture__.

options.text: he shall be late for the lecture
he is late for the lecture
he would be late for the lecture
he may be late for the lecture

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (3).** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option for this underlined segment is **"he would be late for the lecture".**
 
• The given sentence is an indirect speech. "***Professor said"** - Reporting Speech "**that I will be late for the lecture"__- ***Reported Speech
 
• **In "Professor said", 'said' **is a reporting verb. It is in the past tense.
 
• That's why the reported verb must be in the past tense. **'will'** will be changed into **'would'.**
 
• It is clear that the subject of the reported speech is the speaker himself.
 
• That's why in this particular indirect speech the subject** 'I'** will be changed into** 'he'.**
 
• The other options are not in the past tense. They are not appropriate in this context.
 
• Hence the correct answer is option (3)** **i.e. ***"****he would be late for the lecture"*.

Therefore the correct sentence will be **"***Professor said that **__he would be late for the lecture"__***.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Andrew __will playing__ basketball at the college tournament.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is:** is playing.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Present Continuous Tense** is used to describe actions that are happening right now or ongoing.

 
 
• For example: Emma is reading a book right now.
 
 
 
• In this question, "Andrew is playing basketball at the college tournament" implies that Andrew is currently engaged in the activity of playing basketball at this very moment or during a specific time frame in the near future.
 
• Also, **'Andrew' **is a **singular subject.** Hence,** 'is' **(singular verb) must agree with it.

Hence, the correct sentence is: *Andrew **is playing**__ basketball at the college tournament*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**Let's see why the other options are incorrect.

 
• **"are play the": "Are" **is used for **plural subjects**, but Andrew is a **singular subject**. "Play" is not in the present continuous form, which requires "-ing." The word "the" seems misplaced, making the phrase confusing.
 
• **"are play":** Similar to the first incorrect option, "are" is not used for a singular subject like Andrew.
 
• **"is played":** "Andrew is played" would mean someone plays Andrew, which makes no sense in this context.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank.

The athlete’s perseverance and mental toughness ________(facilitate) her to overcome adversity and achieve her goals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2' **i.e.** 'enabled'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **facilitate** means *to make (an action or process) easy or more accessible.* (आसान करना)

 
 
• **For Example** - Schools were located on the same campus to **facilitate** the sharing of resources.
 
 
 
• The word **enabled** means* to make someone able to do something. *(सक्षम बनाना)
 
 
• **For Example** - The grant **enabled** him to study in America.
 
 
 
• So, it is clear that the most appropriate synonym of the word '**Facilitate'** is '**Enable'**.

Therefore, the correct answer to fill in the blank is:** 'enabled'.**

**The correct answer is:** The athlete’s perseverance and mental toughness **enabled__** her to overcome adversity and achieve her goals. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** Let's look at the meaning of the other words given:

 
• **Restricted** means limited in extent, number, scope, or action. (प्रतिबंधित)
 
• **Limited** means restricted in size, amount, or extent; few, small, or short. (सीमित)
 
• **Hindered** means making it difficult for (someone) to do something or for (something) to happen. (बाधा)

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Throughout my career as a journalist, / I covered many important stories and / interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me / to share important information and insights with my readers.

options.text: to share important information and insights with my readers
I covered many important stories and
Throughout my career as a journalist
interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: **interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error in the sentence is found in the segment "interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me".
 
• The correct verb form should align with the noun it refers to. In this case,** "which"** refers to the act of interviewing numerous individuals, a singular concept.
 
• In the sentence, the word "which" refers to the entire **preceding clause**: "I covered many important stories and interviewed numerous individuals."
 
• The use of the singular verb "allows" implies that the combined experiences of covering important stories and interviewing numerous individuals grant the ability to share important information and insights with readers. Therefore, "which" is referring collectively to these journalistic activities.
 
• The verb **"allow" **should therefore be in the singular form to agree with its singular subject, changing to **"allows"**.
 
• Thus, the correct segment should be "interviewed numerous individuals, which allows me".

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *Throughout my career as a journalist, I covered many important stories and interviewed numerous individuals, which allows me to share important information and insights with my readers.*

questions.question:

Oberon doesn’t like the way Demetrius ________ to Helena. (Credit: A Midsummer Night’s Dream)

__
 
• The sentence is derived from William Shakespeare's play "A Midsummer Night's Dream".
 
• **'Talks' **is appropriate for the **singular subject** 'Demetrius,' following the subject-verb agreement rules.
 
• The present simple tense **'talks'** is used to describe habitual actions or general truths. In this context, it indicates Demetrius's ongoing behavior towards Helena.

Therefore, the correct answer is- *Oberon doesn’t like the way Demetrius **talks **__to Helena.*

• **Talked** is the past simple form of 'talk' and would suggest an action that has already been completed.
 
• **Talking** is the gerund form of 'talk,' which would typically be used after prepositions or as the subject of a sentence.
 
• **To talk** is the infinitive form of 'talk,' often used to express purposes or following certain verbs.
